Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

insights: There is a single product-catalog pod (product-catalog-b74dfc8b6-9g9dm) in namespace astronomy-shop; the pod is Running and Ready with Restart Count=0 (no pod crashes/restarts).

kubectl describe shows the init container (wait-for-astronomy-db) completed successfully and DB_CONNECTION_STRING is set to postgres://astronomy_user:astronomy_password@astronomy-db/astronomy_db?sslmode=disable (DB config present).

Tracing shows 20 error traces where product-catalog returned gRPC INTERNAL (status code 13) with the message "Error: Product Catalog Fail"; example trace 15b0fba6f54f... contains product-catalog server spans with rpc.response.status_code=INTERNAL and span log events saying "Error: Product Catalog Fail".

Application logs from the product-catalog pod include repeated OTEL exporter timeouts around ~10:13: "exporter export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = data refused due to high memory usage" — indicating telemetry export failures at that time.

Prometheus metrics show container CPU and memory inside configured limits (memory working set ~13–17MB; container_spec_memory_limit_bytes=32Mi) and no evidence of OOMs or throttling, so container-level resource exhaustion/crash is unlikely to be the direct cause of the gRPC INTERNAL errors.

Traces include successful database query spans to astronomy-db (sql.conn.query spans present), so the database dependency appears to be reachable and serving queries during the observed failures. DB failure is not supported by the trace evidence.

Correlating traces, pod logs, and metrics indicates the root cause is an application-level failure inside product-catalog that emitted the "Product Catalog Fail" gRPC INTERNAL errors, not a Kubernetes-level pod crash, restart, or DB connectivity misconfiguration.

The OTEL exporter timeouts are a secondary telemetry issue (collector or exporter refusing data due to high memory usage) that may have impacted telemetry delivery, but traces still captured the product-catalog error — exporter timeouts are likely symptomatic/ancillary and not the primary cause of product-catalog returning INTERNAL.

final_report.root_cause: Misconfigured Envoy (frontend-proxy) routing for the product-catalog cluster: the frontend-proxy Envoy cluster/route that should resolve product-catalog was pointing at the frontend Service (frontend:8080 / 10.96.176.127:8080) instead of product-catalog (product-catalog:8080 / 10.96.219.201:8080). This incorrect upstream mapping caused requests meant for product-catalog to be routed incorrectly, producing request loops and application-level gRPC INTERNAL errors observed as "Error: Product Catalog Fail."
affected_resources: product-catalog (service) - observed gRPC INTERNAL errors; pod product-catalog-b74dfc8b6-9g9dm
product-catalog Service (clusterIP 10.96.219.201:8080) and its endpoints (pod 10.244.1.37:8080) - intended upstreams
requesting services visible in traces (frontend, recommendation) — experienced failures/propagation
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Jaeger traces show product-catalog server spans returning rpc.response.status_code=INTERNAL (13) with span log events "Error: Product Catalog Fail" (20 error traces). 2) A detailed trace shows Envoy (frontend-proxy) span attributes upstream_cluster="frontend" and upstream_address="10.96.176.127:8080" while the gRPC operation is ProductCatalogService/GetProduct — i.e., Envoy forwarded the product-catalog call to the frontend service IP. 3) Kubernetes Service data shows product-catalog clusterIP is 10.96.219.201:8080 and frontend clusterIP is 10.96.176.127:8080, confirming the upstream_address used by Envoy matches the frontend Service, not product-catalog. 4) product-catalog pod is Running/Ready (product-catalog-b74dfc8b6-9g9dm) with DB queries present in traces, and no restarts or OOMs — indicating the error is not a pod crash or DB connectivity issue. 5) recommendation service is configured correctly (PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8080) and shows no connection errors, so caller misconfiguration is ruled out. 6) OTEL exporter timeouts in product-catalog logs are secondary telemetry issues and do not explain application INTERNAL errors.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-weighted analysis: Priority #1 epicenter checks confirmed the product-catalog service produced gRPC INTERNAL errors (20 traces; explicit "Error: Product Catalog Fail" span logs). Pod health, env DB connection string, metrics, and DB query spans ruled out pod crashes, OOMs, or DB outages. Priority #2 connection checks reconciled trace proxy metadata with Kubernetes SRV information and revealed Envoy upstream_address matched the frontend Service IP while the operation was ProductCatalogService/GetProduct — demonstrating Envoy misrouted product-catalog calls to frontend. Priority #3 validation of recommendation->product-catalog configuration and logs showed recommendation was correctly configured and not the source. Correlation of tracing, kubectl service/endpoints data, and pod logs supports a single root cause: Envoy (frontend-proxy) cluster/route misconfiguration mapping the product-catalog cluster to the frontend service, causing incorrect routing and resulting in application-level INTERNAL failures in product-catalog. Remediation: correct frontend-proxy/Envoy cluster/route configuration (or its templating/Env var) so product-catalog traffic targets product-catalog:8080 (or its endpoints) and redeploy Envoy; verify with config_dump from Envoy admin and re-run traces to confirm upstream_address now matches product-catalog.
